reason: This passage emphasizes mutual love and equality between Jonathan and David rather than hierarchy. Despite their different social positions (Jonathan as king's son, David as a servant), the text portrays their relationship as one of profound equality: their souls are 'bound together' (נקשרה בנפש), Jonathan loves David 'as his own soul' (כנפשו), and they make a mutual covenant. Notably, Jonathan actually subverts hierarchy by removing his royal garments and symbols of power (robe, sword, bow, belt) and giving them to David. Furthermore, Jonathan actively resists and works against his father's hierarchical authority to protect David. The passage consistently emphasizes their bond as one of reciprocal devotion rather than hierarchical relationship.
